nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: Out on the street you think: the book. You can’t really have left something you never found.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: Out of school. Looking back, I can’t tell which windows belong to the classroom.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You turn to get a look at the wall. From this side the classroom windows look like all the others.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: There are more buildings across the road. Follow the pavement; there’ll be somewhere to cross.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The tiles stop in a neat line below the windows. You’d have to count further up to get to where you were sitting.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The camera points at a patch of grass instead of the door. Whoever watches it wouldn’t know when class let out.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: The school camera is aimed at the grass, not the door.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: If you do come back, the windows won’t help.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You left the tab on the glass side. Follow the wall to the glass. Decide which floor it is when you get to the door.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You left the tab on the stair side. These steps outside aren’t the ones. That mark is only any use once you’ve gone in.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: There’s a sheet under this one. Where the top corner curls you can see half an old photo.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: Lost cat. One crouching in the top photo, a bit of tail in the one underneath. Try fitting them together. They don’t go.

effects.speaker: protagonist
effects.text: Two lost-cat notices layered on the pole. The parts of the photos you can see don’t match.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The date on the bottom sheet is the clearest part. Four years ago. The outer tape is still tacky.
